messages:
alex: Customer reports being dropped to login after MFA when switching apps on Android. Happens only in our in-app WebView flow, not system browser. Said it works briefly then forces reauth after app is backgrounded.
maria_support: Thanks — can you paste repro steps and device/os version? Do we have a customer id or session trace? :thinking_face:
alex: Repro steps from customer: 1) Open app, login via in-app WebView SSO + MFA 2) Complete OTP 3) Press home to background app for ~10s 4) Reopen app -> sees login screen. Device: Pixel 6 / Android 13, app v2.4.1. They attached logs but redacted.
jamal_eng: Possibility: WebView cookie store or native cookie sync not persisting refresh token / set-cookie lifecycle. Also many WebViews clear ephemeral cookie jars when process is killed. Do we rotate refresh tokens on login that could be invalidated by a parallel refresh call on resume?
oscar_mobile: We've seen similar on older Chromium WebViews — cookie manager isn't automatically persisted unless you call CookieManager.flush(). Also our Android code uses a short window where we exchange the auth code for tokens and immediately rotate refresh token. If WebView resumes and triggers a silent refresh at the same time, it can race and cause the refresh token the app holds to be rejected.
alex: Customer logs show repeated 401 from /oauth/token after resume. Snippet they provided:
```
I/flutter (12345): [auth] resume: starting silent refresh
I/flutter (12345): [http] POST /oauth/token -> 401 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Refresh token invalid"}
I/flutter (12345): [auth] fallback to interactive
```
jamal_eng: That lines up. Two notable issues to investigate: 1) race on refresh-token rotation (server invalidates prior RT when rotating) 2) WebView cookie persistence / SameSite attributes preventing cookie from being reapplied on resume.
maria_support: Customer asked for workaround until fix — what's safe to recommend? They are in production.
oscar_mobile: Short-term mitigations: a) switch to system browser (CustomTabs) for auth to avoid WebView cookie edge cases; b) on resume, delay any silent refresh by ~500ms and serialize refresh requests with a lock; c) ensure CookieManager.flush() after the login exchange to persist cookies to disk.
jamal_eng: From the platform side we can add a tolerance: when rotating refresh tokens, keep the previous token valid for a short overlap window (e.g., 30s) to tolerate races. That buys time while mobile teams roll out clients.
infra-bot: New ticket created: INFRA-4802 — Investigate RT rotation overlap policy for WebView clients.
alex: I'll reply to the customer with steps: try CustomTabs if feasible, update app to call CookieManager.flush() after login, and add the resume delay as a hotfix. Also ask for full DEBUG logs and the network trace for /oauth/token. :thumbsup:
maria_support: Customer replied: "We can try CustomTabs but it's a big change. Can you put the server-side overlap in place while we ship a smaller hotfix?" They asked for ETA.
jamal_eng: I'll scope it: implement short overlap acceptance for rotated refresh tokens -> can be done as a config flag behind a rollout gate. ETA: 2 dev days + QA. Will coordinate with infra for a controlled rollout. No change to access tokens.
oscar_mobile: I'll propose a minimal client hotfix (CookieManager.flush() + retry serialization) — one day for a patch release.
alex: Great. I'll set expectations with the customer: server-side overlap (2d), client hotfix (1d), recommend CustomTabs as long-term. Will collect logs now.
maria_support: Thanks team — tagging customer and scheduling follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
